method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: SLE flare vs infection: distinguishing features, complement, anti-dsDNA, CRP
topic.coverageNote: Uses complement and anti-dsDNA as markers that do not track CRP, plus the ESR:CRP ratio. It is a cohort study, not a diagnostic guideline.

mcqs.question: How does CRP relate to anti-dsDNA and complement in the background cited here?

options.A: CRP does not tend to correlate with anti-dsDNA or complement
options.B: CRP falls whenever anti-dsDNA rises, in a fixed ratio
options.C: Complement and CRP always move together
options.E: The paper says CRP replaces complement testing

mcqs.correctAnswerText: CRP does not tend to correlate with anti-dsDNA or complement
mcqs.explanation: CRP levels do not tend to correlate with anti-dsDNA antibodies or complement levels.

sourceRefs.excerpt: CRP levels do not tend to correlate with other markers of disease activity such as anti-double stranded DNA antibodies and complement levels

mcqs.question: Which CRP threshold has been associated with infection in SLE in the studies this paper cites?

options.D: CRP is never raised in infection
options.E: Only ESR, not CRP, has been linked to infection

mcqs.explanation: CRP values above 6.0 mg/dl in SLE have been associated with infectious processes in several studies, and CRP is higher in infection than in flare without infection.

sourceRefs.excerpt: CRP values of >6.0 mg/dl in SLE patients have been associated with infectious processes in several studies

mcqs.question: In this series, which ESR:CRP ratios pointed toward infection versus flare?

options.A: Infection predominated at ≤2 and flare at ≥15
options.B: Flare predominated at ≤2 and infection at ≥15
options.E: A ratio of 2 diagnosed lupus nephritis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Infection predominated at ≤2 and flare at ≥15
mcqs.explanation: Infections predominated when the ESR:CRP ratio was 2 or lower, and flares predominated at ratios of 15 or higher.

sourceRefs.excerpt: infections predominant for ratios of ≤2, and flares predominant for ratios of ≥15; p<0.000

mcqs.question: Which flare features were associated with higher CRP?

options.A: Serosal flares had higher CRP than flares without serositis
options.B: Arthritis flares had the highest CRP in every comparison
options.D: Myositis flares had undetectable CRP by definition
options.E: CRP was identical in all flare types

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Serosal flares had higher CRP than flares without serositis
mcqs.explanation: The 10 flares with a serosal component had higher CRP than the 18 without (8.7±8.3 versus 3.6±4.6, p=0.04).

sourceRefs.excerpt: CRP levels were higher for the 10 flares with a serosal component compared to the 18 flares without a serosal component [8.7 ±8.3 vs 3.6 ±4.6 (p=0.04)

mcqs.question: Why do the authors say a flare-versus-infection distinction matters before immunosuppression?

options.A: High-dose glucocorticoids and other immunosuppression can be dangerous if the process is infection
options.E: ESR must be normalized before any culture

mcqs.correctAnswerText: High-dose glucocorticoids and other immunosuppression can be dangerous if the process is infection
mcqs.explanation: Presumptive flare treatment with immunosuppressants, including high-dose glucocorticoids, can be dangerous if infection is present, so aggressive immunosuppression is usually postponed until infection is excluded.

sourceRefs.excerpt: presumptive treatment of SLE flares with immunosuppressive medications, including high dose glucocorticoids, can be dangerous in the setting of an infection
